newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government in censure motion challenges.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government in censure motion challenges.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government faced several challenges to its precarious rule on Tuesday in parliamentary wrangling over a planned vote of confidence, parliament officials said.

Parliament's advisory committee was to meet at 11 a.m. (0800 GMT) to consider an opposition request for a censure motion to be held later in the day against Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition.
Even if it fails at the committee stage, the opposition is expected to ask a full parliamentary session at 3 p.m. (1200 GMT) for two separate votes on whether to hold the censure motion immediately.
Under Turkish parliamentary tradition, the government would resign if it lost either of the two votes. The opposition says Erbakan has damaged Turkey's secularism with a series of Islamist proposals.
A deputy from Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party defected to the main opposition Motherland Party on Monday, cutting the coalition's narrow majority in parliament.
Erbakan's administration has 280 seats -- of a necessary 276 -- in the 550-member assembly but several MPs in his True Path Party coalition partner are uneasy at the government's Islamist hue.
"The preliminary censure motion debate will take place in parliament today," said Welfare Party deputy Salih Kapusuz, who is also on the parliament's advisory committee.
The advisory committee met earlier on Tuesday to consider the motion filed against Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his cabinet.

After Tuesday's debate, parliament will vote on whether to hold a full censure vote later this month. The government is not technically over if it loses this vote, but under Turkish parliamentary tradition the government would resign following a defeat.

The Islamist-led government, which has 280 seats in the 550-seat parliament, has survived three censure motions since it was formed in June. The opposition has said it expects many government MPs to support the motion.
